title: The flat base change map on sections: pullback of cohomology classes
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:S'\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with fibre product $X'=S'\times_SX$ [def-pc-fibre-product], projections $f':X'\to S'$, $g':X'\to X$, and assume $g$ and $g'$ flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $\mathcal F'=g'^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] and $p\ge0$. Choose injective resolutions $a:\mathcal F[0]\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ and $b:\mathcal F'[0]\to\mathcal J^\bullet$, zero in negative degrees [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Write $\mathcal F'=g'^*\mathcal F$ and choose a chain map $t:\mathcal I^\bullet\to g'_*\mathcal J^\bullet$ satisfying $ta=g'_*(b)\eta_{\mathcal F}$, with $\eta$ the pullback adjunction unit [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $A=f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$, $B=f'_*\mathcal J^\bullet$ and $q=f_*t:A\to g_*B$ (the equality $f_*g'_*=g_*f'_*$ is the sectionwise equality from the square). Define $c:g^*A\to B$ to be the termwise adjoint of $q$, and $\beta=\mathcal H^p(c):g^*R^pf_*\mathcal F\to R^pf'_*\mathcal F'$, using exactness of $g^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective]. Define $\beta^\flat$ to be the adjoint of $\beta$; these maps are independent of the resolutions and lifts. Then, under the descriptions of $R^pf_*\mathcal F$ and $R^pf'_*\mathcal F'$ as sheafified presheaves [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf], $\beta^\flat$ is the morphism induced by the maps of presheaves $H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)\to H^p(f'^{-1}(g^{-1}(V)),\mathcal F')$, $V\subseteq S$ open, given by the pullback along $g'|:f'^{-1}(g^{-1}(V))=g'^{-1}(f^{-1}(V))\to f^{-1}(V)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (a) (with $(g'|)^*(\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}V})=\mathcal F'|_{g'^{-1}f^{-1}V}$): for $\xi\in H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)$ with image $[\xi]\in(R^pf_*\mathcal F)(V)$, $\beta^\flat_V([\xi])$ is the image of $(g'|)^*\xi$ in $(R^pf'_*\mathcal F')(g^{-1}(V))$.

proof.text: Injective resolutions exist by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective], each $g'_*\mathcal J^n$ is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] to the degreewise monic quasi-isomorphism $a:\mathcal F[0]\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ and the chain map $g'_*(b)\eta_{\mathcal F}$ to obtain $t$; the augmentation is monic by exactness of the resolution. [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] makes two choices homotopic. On an open $V\subseteq S$, $(f_*g'_*\mathcal J^n)(V)=\mathcal J^n(g'{}^{-1}f^{-1}V)=\mathcal J^n(f'{}^{-1}g^{-1}V)=(g_*f'_*\mathcal J^n)(V)$; the equality respects restrictions and differentials. The adjunction of [def-pc-module-pullback] therefore defines $c$. It preserves homotopies termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Comparison lifts between two injective resolutions, and their composites, are homotopy inverse by the same lift and uniqueness nodes. Composing $t$ with these lifts gives the same augmented map up to homotopy, so the construction is also independent of resolutions.

proof.text: Put $U=f^{-1}V$, $W=g'{}^{-1}U=f'{}^{-1}g^{-1}V$ and $h=g'|_W:W\to U$. Both restricted augmentations are injective resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives]. Restriction of $t$ is a chain map $t_U:\mathcal I^\bullet|_U\to h_*(\mathcal J^\bullet|_W)$ with $t_Ua|_U=h_*(b|_W)\eta_{\mathcal F|_U}$. Indeed the unit on an open $T\subseteq U$ sends $x\in\mathcal F(T)$ to $1\otimes x$ in the pullback over $h^{-1}T$; restricting the original unit gives that same tensor. The identification $h^*(\mathcal F|_U)=(g'{}^*\mathcal F)|_W$ follows directly from the tensor/inverse-image definition [def-pc-module-pullback]: on $W$ the ring sheaves and inverse-image sheaves in both tensors coincide (the opens of $U$ are cofinal near each point mapping into $U$). Thus no unspecified transport of cohomology is being used.

proof.text: For every $V$ the chain map of sections is explicitly $q_V^n=t_U^n(U):\mathcal I^n(U)\to\mathcal J^n(W)$. To compute the pullback $h^*$ in [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (a), use these restricted resolutions and choose a quasi-isomorphism $\lambda:h_*(\mathcal J^\bullet|_W)\to L^\bullet$ into injectives. It exists by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono]. The comparison map in that definition can be chosen as $\lambda t_U$, since its composite with $a|_U$ is precisely the prescribed augmented map. Write $\mu=\Gamma(U,\lambda)$, identifying $\Gamma(U,h_*\mathcal J|_W)=\Gamma(W,\mathcal J|_W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injectives-sections-quasi-iso], $H^p(\mu)$ is invertible. The defining formula is consequently $h^*=H^p(\mu)^{-1}H^p(\mu q_V)=H^p(q_V)$. In particular a cocycle $s\in\mathcal I^p(U)$ representing $\xi$ maps to the cocycle $t_U^p(U)(s)\in\mathcal J^p(W)$.

source.place: 01FB, remark-explain-arrow, diagram equation-choice and definition of the cohomology arrow; 01EZ, lemma-before-Leray; applied here to the restricted resolutions from step 2

proof.text: If $V_0\subseteq V$, put $U_0=f^{-1}V_0$ and $W_0=g'{}^{-1}U_0$. Since $t^n$ is a sheaf morphism, $\operatorname{res}^{W}_{W_0}q_V^n=q_{V_0}^n\operatorname{res}^{U}_{U_0}$ in each degree. Restrictions on cohomology are the maps of these section complexes: use the restricted resolutions and the identity comparison in [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b), justified by [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives]. Thus the $H^p(q_V)$ form a presheaf map into $V\mapsto(R^pf'_*\mathcal F')(g^{-1}V)$ after the canonical maps $\theta'$ of [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf]. This target is a sheaf by the direct-image definition. Sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives a unique sheaf morphism $m:R^pf_*\mathcal F\to g_*R^pf'_*\mathcal F'$ with $m_V\theta_V=\theta'_{g^{-1}V}H^p(q_V)$.

source.place: 01E4, lemma-describe-higher-direct-images, presheaf restriction maps and sheafification; 01FB, remark-explain-arrow; the degreewise restriction square is written out by the agent

proof.text: Finally $q=g_*c\,\eta_A$ by adjunction. Locally every section of $\mathcal H^p(A)$ is represented by a cocycle $s$ of $A^p$, by [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf]. Exactness of $g^*$ identifies $g^*\mathcal H^p(A)$ with $\mathcal H^p(g^*A)$: kernels and images are preserved. On the corresponding local class the unit sends $[s]$ to the class of $\eta_A(s)$, and $\mathcal H^p(c)$ then sends it to $[c\eta_A(s)]=[q(s)]$. Hence the adjoint $\beta^\flat$ satisfies $\beta^\flat_V\theta_V(\xi)=\theta'_{g^{-1}V}H^p(q_V)(\xi)$, the same formula defining $m$; uniqueness of sheafification gives $\beta^\flat=m$. Step 3 substitutes $H^p(q_V)=h^*$, proving the stated formula.
